evidence.quote: [/page/0/Text/9] Fifty-nine high school students, aged 14-18, meeting DSM-III and RDC criteria for a diagnosis of depression were randomly assigned to one of three conditions: Adolescent-and-Parent, Adolescent-Only, and Wait-List.

[/page/2/Text/5] Subjects in each cohort were randomly assigned to one of three conditions: (a) Adolescent-Only, a cognitive-behavioral psychoeducational group for adolescents only (N = 19); (b) Adolescent-and-Parent, an identical group for adolescents with their parents enrolled in a separate parent group (N = 21); and (c) a wait-list condition (N = 19).

[page/7/Text/7] The K-SADS-E interview data indicated a substantial decrease in the percent meeting criteria for a diagnosis of depression from pre to posttreatment in the two active treatment conditions (Chi square (2, N = 59) = 9.41; p < .01).
[/page/9/Text/4] Adolescent-Only, N = 21; Adolescent-and-Parent, N = 19; Wait List, N = 19.

[/page/0/Text/9] The treatments were: a) an adaptation of the Coping with Depression Course (CWD), a cognitive-behavioral group intervention teaching skills for increasing pleasant activities, relaxation, controlling depressive thoughts, improving social interaction, and communication, negotiation and conflict resolution skills;
[/page/2/Text/5] (a) Adolescent-Only, a cognitive-behavioral psychoeducational group for adolescents only
